about: Macro-driven, concentrated bets that change quickly.
summary: 86 holdings; the top ten are 52% of the portfolio.
Trades a lot: about 159% of the portfolio changes in a year.
The average holding, by value, has been owned for 1.6 years.
Compared with the typical S&P 500 company, its holdings are similarly priced, more profitable, faster-growing and much larger.
Copying each filing beat the S&P 500 in 5 of 9 full years.

profile.background: Born in 1953. Founded Duquesne Capital in 1981 and also managed George Soros's Quantum Fund from 1988 to 2000. Closed Duquesne to outside money in 2010 and now invests his own family's money.
profile.approach: Top-down: forms a view of the economy and markets, then makes large, concentrated bets that can change quickly, across stocks, bonds and currencies.
known: With Soros, bet against the British pound in 1992 (Black Wednesday), reputedly making over $1 billion.
Duquesne is reported to have averaged about 30% a year without a losing year.
profile.note: A family office: the 13F shows only US shares, not his bond, currency or futures positions.

name: Stanley Druckenmiller
